title: Quotient data before local elimination in desingularization
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], Λ an R-algebra, A a finitely presented R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], π∈R, and α:A→Λ an R-algebra map. Assume Ann_Λ(π)=Ann_Λ(π²), the image of π in A is strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element], and there is an R-algebra section ρ:A/π⁴A→R/π⁴R compatible with α modulo π⁴. Then there is a finitely presented R-algebra S and an ideal K of S such that K⊆(π²), (π)K⊆K², and S/K is finitely presented. There are R-algebra maps aB:A→S/K and β:S/K→Λ with β∘aB=α. The principal localization (S/K)_π is smooth over R. At every prime p of S containing π, R→S is smooth at p [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] and S_p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is flat over R [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The conclusion does not assert any smoothness of S/K at primes containing π.

source.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Presentation. By (1) and the definition of strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] there are a presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], i.e. an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\theta:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ ($f_j\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]), and an integer $0\le c\le\min(n,m)$ such that (i) $\pi=\sum_{I\subset\{1,\dots,n\},|I|=c}a_I\,\theta\big(\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j=1,\dots,c,\ i\in I}\big)$ in $A$ for some $a_I\in A$ ($\partial/\partial x_i$ the formal partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]; $\theta(P)$ means $\theta$ of the class of $P$), and (ii) $\pi f_{c+j}\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)+(f_1,\dots,f_m)^2$ in $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ for $j=1,\dots,m-c$. Write $\rho$ for the map of (2) and $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ for the given map; for $y\in A$ write $\bar y$ for its class in $A/\pi^4A$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1682-1691 (choice of the presentation and of c with (equation-strictly-standard-one) and (equation-star))

proof.text: Translation of the variables (Stacks: 'we can replace $x_i$ by $x_i-r_i$'). Choose $r_i\in R$ with $\rho(\overline{\theta(x_i)})=r_i\bmod\pi^4$ ($R/\pi^4R$ is a quotient of $R$). Let $\sigma$ be the $R$-algebra endomorphism of $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with $\sigma(x_i)=x_i+r_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; it is an automorphism with inverse $x_i\mapsto x_i-r_i$ (the composites fix every $x_i$, so are the identity by the uniqueness in the universal property). Put $f'_j=\sigma(f_j)$. Then $\sigma$ maps the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ onto $(f'_1,\dots,f'_m)$ and induces an isomorphism $\bar\sigma:R[x]/(f)\to R[x]/(f')$, so $\theta'=\theta\circ\bar\sigma^{-1}:R[x]/(f')\to A$ is again a presentation, with $\theta'(P)=\theta(\sigma^{-1}P)$, hence $\theta'(\sigma Q)=\theta(Q)$ for all $Q$, and $\theta'(x_i)=\theta(x_i)-r_i$, so $\rho(\overline{\theta'(x_i)})=0$. Derivatives: $\partial(\sigma Q)/\partial x_i=\sigma(\partial Q/\partial x_i)$ for all $Q$. Indeed $D_1=\partial_i\circ\sigma$ and $D_2=\sigma\circ\partial_i$ are $R$-linear and both satisfy $D(PQ)=\sigma(P)D(Q)+\sigma(Q)D(P)$ (Leibniz rule of [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] and multiplicativity of $\sigma$); $D_1(1)=D_2(1)=0$ and $D_1(x_k)=\partial(x_k+r_k)/\partial x_i=\delta_{ik}=\sigma(\delta_{ik})=D_2(x_k)$; by induction on the degree they agree on all monomials, hence everywhere by $R$-linearity. Therefore $\theta'\big(\det(\partial f'_j/\partial x_i)_{j\le c,i\in I}\big)=\theta'\big(\sigma\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j\le c,i\in I}\big)=\theta\big(\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j\le c,i\in I}\big)$ ($\sigma$ is a ring map and the determinant a polynomial in the entries), so (i) holds for $(f',\theta')$ with the same $a_I$; applying $\sigma$ to a relation $\pi f_{c+j}=\sum_{k\le c}a_kf_k+\sum_{l\le l'}b_{ll'}f_lf_{l'}$ gives (ii) for $f'$. From now on we write $f_j,\theta$ for $f'_j,\theta'$ and $x_i$ also for $\theta(x_i)\in A$; thus $\rho(\bar x_i)=0$ for all $i$. Consequences: (a) $\rho\circ(A\to A/\pi^4A)$ is an $R$-algebra map $A\to R/\pi^4R$ killing every $x_i$, so it sends $\theta(P)$ to $P(0)\bmod\pi^4$ for every $P\in R[x]$ (both are $R$-algebra maps $R[x]\to R/\pi^4R$ agreeing on the $x_i$); applied to $\theta(f_j)=0$ this gives $f_j(0)\in\pi^4R$. (b) By the compatibility in (2), the class of $\alpha(x_i)$ in $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ is the image of $\rho(\bar x_i)=0$, so $\alpha(x_i)=\pi^4\lambda_i$ for some $\lambda_i\in\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1692-1697 ('Say rho maps x_i to the class of r_i ... A -> Lambda maps x_i to pi^4 lambda_i')

proof.text: Linear terms and the unit $u$. Let $r_{ji}\in R$ be the coefficient of $x_i$ in $f_j$; write $f_j=f_j(0)+\sum_{i=1}^nr_{ji}x_i+Q_j$ with $Q_j$ a sum of monomials of degree $\ge2$, i.e. $Q_j\in(x_1,\dots,x_n)^2$. By the explicit formula of [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] the constant term of $\partial f_j/\partial x_i$ is $r_{ji}$ (a monomial $rx^e$ contributes a constant only if $e$ is the $i$-th unit vector). Apply $\rho$ to (i): by Step 2(a), $\rho(\bar\pi)=\pi\bmod\pi^4$ and $\rho$ sends the image of $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j\le c,i\in I}$ to $\det(r_{ji})_{j\le c,i\in I}\bmod\pi^4$; choosing $r_I\in R$ with $\rho(\bar a_I)=r_I\bmod\pi^4$ we get $\pi=\sum_{|I|=c}r_I\det(r_{ji})_{j=1,\dots,c,\ i\in I}+\pi^4t$ for some $t\in R$. Put $u=1-\pi^3t\in1+\pi^3R$; then $u\pi=\sum_{|I|=c}r_I\det(r_{ji})_{j\le c,\,i\in I}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1697-1714 ('Write f_j = f_j(0) + sum r_ji x_i + h.o.t. ... for some u in 1 + pi^3 R')

proof.text: The matrix $(s_{ik})$. Let $M$ be the $n\times c$ matrix over $R$ with entries $M_{ij}=r_{ji}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $1\le j\le c$); $n\ge c$. For $I\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$, $|I|=c$, the submatrix $M_I$ of the rows with index in $I$ is the transpose of $(r_{ji})_{j\le c,i\in I}$, so $\det M_I=\det(r_{ji})_{j\le c,i\in I}$ (a determinant equals that of its transpose). By Step 3, $u\pi$ lies in the ideal generated by the $c\times c$ minors of $M$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors](1) there is a $c\times n$ matrix $S'$ with $S'M=u\pi\cdot1_{c\times c}$. With $s_{ik}=S'_{ki}$ this reads $\sum_{i=1}^nr_{ji}s_{ik}=u\pi\,\delta_{jk}$ for all $j,k=1,\dots,c$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1715-1722 (Algebra, Lemma 07DQ, lemma-matrix-left-inverse)

proof.text: The elements $h_i$, $g_j$, $\varphi_j$. Let $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,v_1,\dots,v_c,w_1,\dots,w_n]$ and $\xi_i=\pi^2\sum_{k=1}^cs_{ik}v_k+\pi^3w_i\in R[v,w]$, $h_i=x_i-\xi_i\in P$. (a) Elimination: the $R$-algebra map $\epsilon:P\to R[v,w]$, $x_i\mapsto\xi_i$, $v\mapsto v$, $w\mapsto w$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], is surjective with kernel $(h_1,\dots,h_n)$: it kills the $h_i$, and $F-\epsilon(F)\in(h_1,\dots,h_n)$ for every $F\in P$ (true for $x_i$, $v_k$, $w_i$, and the set of such $F$ is closed under sums and products since $FG-\epsilon(F)\epsilon(G)=F(G-\epsilon G)+\epsilon(G)(F-\epsilon F)$); hence $P/(h)\cong R[v,w]$, and for every $F\in R[x]$, $F-F(\xi)\in(h)$. (b) Computation of $f_j(\xi)=\epsilon(f_j)$: since $\xi_i\in\pi^2R[v,w]$, $Q_j(\xi)\in(\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n)^2\subset\pi^4R[v,w]$, and $f_j(0)\in\pi^4R$ (Step 2(a)); hence $f_j(\xi)\equiv\sum_ir_{ji}\xi_i=\pi^2\sum_{k=1}^c\big(\sum_ir_{ji}s_{ik}\big)v_k+\pi^3\sum_ir_{ji}w_i\pmod{\pi^4R[v,w]}$. For $j\le c$, Step 4 gives $\pi^2\sum_k(\sum_ir_{ji}s_{ik})v_k=u\pi^3v_j=\pi^3v_j+(u-1)\pi^3v_j$ with $(u-1)\pi^3\in\pi^6R$; so $f_j(\xi)=\pi^3\big(v_j+\sum_ir_{ji}w_i\big)+\pi^4e_j$ for some $e_j\in R[v,w]$. Put $g_j=v_j+\sum_{i=1}^nr_{ji}w_i+\pi e_j\in R[v,w]\subset P$ ($j=1,\dots,c$). Then $f_j(\xi)=\pi^3g_j$ in $R[v,w]$, $g_j\equiv v_j+\sum_ir_{ji}w_i\pmod\pi$, and by (a) $f_j-\pi^3g_j\in(h_1,\dots,h_n)$ in $P$. (c) For every $j$ (in particular $j>c$) each term of $f_j(0)+\sum_ir_{ji}\xi_i+Q_j(\xi)$ lies in $\pi^2R[v,w]$, so $f_j(\xi)=\pi^2\varphi_j$ for some $\varphi_j\in R[v,w]$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1723-1754 (the h_i, 'without further mention', the computation of f_j mod pi^4 and the choice of g_j)

proof.text: The algebra $B$ and the factorization. Put $B=P/(f_1,\dots,f_m,h_1,\dots,h_n,g_1,\dots,g_c)$: $2n+c$ variables and $m+n+c$ relations, so $B$ is of finite presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. The $R$-algebra map $R[x]\to B$, $x_i\mapsto x_i$, kills the $f_j$ and so gives $A\cong R[x]/(f)\to B$. Define the $R$-algebra map $P\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] by $x_i\mapsto\pi^4\lambda_i=\alpha(x_i)$ (Step 2(b)), $v_k\mapsto0$, $w_i\mapsto\pi\lambda_i$. It kills $f_j$ (the image is $f_j(\alpha(x_1),\dots,\alpha(x_n))=\alpha(\theta(f_j))=0$) and $h_i$ (image $\pi^4\lambda_i-0-\pi^3\pi\lambda_i=0$). Let $t_j$ be the image of $g_j$. As $f_j-\pi^3g_j\in(h)$ (Step 5(b)), $\pi^3t_j=0$; as $g_j=v_j+\sum_ir_{ji}w_i+\pi e_j$, $t_j=\pi\sum_ir_{ji}\lambda_i+\pi e_j(0,\pi\lambda)=\pi\mu_j$ with $\mu_j\in\Lambda$, so $\pi^4\mu_j=0$. From $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^2)$ one gets $\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi^k)=\mathrm{Ann}_\Lambda(\pi)$ for all $k\ge1$ by induction (if $\pi^{k+1}y=0$ then $\pi^{k-1}y\in\mathrm{Ann}(\pi^2)=\mathrm{Ann}(\pi)$, so $\pi^ky=0$); so $\pi\mu_j=0$, i.e. $t_j=0$. Hence $P\to\Lambda$ factors through $\beta:B\to\Lambda$. The composite $A\to B\to\Lambda$ sends $x_i$ to $\pi^4\lambda_i=\alpha(x_i)$; since $A$ is generated by the $x_i$ as an $R$-algebra, it equals $\alpha$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1755-1772 ('We set B = ... Thus we are done if we can prove the statement about smoothness')

proof.text: $B_\pi$ is smooth over $R$. In $P/(f,h)$ we have $\pi^3g_j=f_j-(f_j-\pi^3g_j)=0$ for $j\le c$ (Step 5(b)), so $g_j/1=0$ in $(P/(f,h))_\pi$ and, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] (with the ideal generated by the $g_j$), $B_\pi\cong(P/(f,h))_\pi$. Next $P/(f)\cong A[v,w]$, the polynomial ring over $A\cong R[x]/(f)$ (both have the universal property of $R$-algebra maps out of $R[x,v,w]$ killing the $f_j$), so $P/(f,h)\cong A[v,w]/(\bar h_1,\dots,\bar h_n)$ with $\bar h_i=x_i-\pi^2\sum_ks_{ik}v_k-\pi^3w_i$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] again, together with $A[v,w]_\pi=A_\pi[v,w]$ (same universal property), $(P/(f,h))_\pi\cong A_\pi[v,w]/(\bar h)$. In $A_\pi[v,w]$, $\bar h_i=-\pi^3(w_i-\zeta_i)$ with $\zeta_i=\pi^{-3}(x_i-\pi^2\sum_ks_{ik}v_k)\in A_\pi[v]$ and $\pi^3$ a unit, so $(\bar h)=(w_1-\zeta_1,\dots,w_n-\zeta_n)$, and by the elimination argument of Step 5(a) $A_\pi[v,w]/(w_i-\zeta_i)\cong A_\pi[v_1,\dots,v_c]$. Thus $B_\pi\cong A_\pi[v_1,\dots,v_c]$ as $R$-algebras. Since $\pi$ is strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ (1), $A_\pi$ is smooth over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-localization-smooth]; $A_\pi\to A_\pi[v_1,\dots,v_c]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]; so $R\to A_\pi[v]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](2), and so is the isomorphic $R$-algebra $B_\pi$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Consequently $R\to B$ is smooth at every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ with $\pi\notin\mathfrak q$ (take $g=\pi$ in [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1774-1779 ('Note that B_pi = A_pi[v_1,...,v_c] ... see Lemma 07CA (lemma-elkik)')

proof.text: The algebra $B'$ and $B$ as its quotient. Put $B'=R[v_1,\dots,v_c,w_1,\dots,w_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_c)$, of finite presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. By Step 5(a), $B=P/(f,h,g)\cong R[v,w]/(f_1(\xi),\dots,f_m(\xi),g_1,\dots,g_c)$, and since $f_j(\xi)=\pi^3g_j$ for $j\le c$ (Step 5(b)) this is $B'/K$ with $K=(\tilde f_{c+1},\dots,\tilde f_m)$, $\tilde f_l$ the class of $f_l(\xi)$ in $B'$; the surjection $B'\to B$ is $v\mapsto v$, $w\mapsto w$. Also $\tilde f_l=\pi^2\tilde\varphi_l$ (Step 5(c)). Applying the substitution $x\mapsto\xi$ (an $R$-algebra map) to (ii), written as $\pi f_{c+j}=\sum_{k\le c}a_{jk}f_k+\sum_{l\le l'}b_{jll'}f_lf_{l'}$ ($a,b\in R[x]$; $(f)^2$ is generated by the products $f_lf_{l'}$), and using $f_k(\xi)=\pi^3g_k=0$ in $B'$ for $k\le c$, we get in $B'$: $\pi\tilde f_{c+j}=\sum_{c<l\le l'}b_{jll'}(\xi)\tilde f_l\tilde f_{l'}$ for $j=1,\dots,m-c$. Consequently K is contained in the principal ideal (π²), and (π)K is contained in K². Both S=B′ and S/K=B are finitely presented; an ULift preserves their algebra structures, presentations and localization properties and puts S in Type(max u w).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1781-1795 (B', 'B_q is the quotient of B'_{q'} by the ideal generated by f_{c+j}', the two observations)

proof.text: $R\to B'$ is smooth, and flat, at every prime $\mathfrak q'\subset B'$ with $\pi\in\mathfrak q'$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak q'$, so $\pi\in\mathfrak p$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ its residue field and $F=B'\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] (with $R'=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$), $F\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)[v,w]/(\bar g_1,\dots,\bar g_c)$ with $\bar g_j$ the image of $g_j$ under coefficient reduction; as $\pi\mapsto0$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\bar g_j=v_j+\sum_i\bar r_{ji}w_i$. With the variables ordered $(v_1,\dots,v_c,w_1,\dots,w_n)$, $N=n+c\ge c$, we have $\det(\partial\bar g_j/\partial v_k)_{j,k\le c}=\det(1_c)=1$, a unit; so this is a standard smooth presentation of $F$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of relative dimension $n$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. Hence (a) $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}\operatorname{Spec}F=N-c=n$ [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-over-field-dimension-at-points] (the dimension of the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ at $\mathfrak Q$ of [def-kun-dimension] is by definition that of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}F$ at $\mathfrak Q$ of [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]); (b) $F$ is smooth over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth], so $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q$ ($g=1$ in [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]). As $B'=R[y_1,\dots,y_N]/(g_1,\dots,g_c)$ with $N-c=n$, (a) and [lem-weil-pbc-equation-count-fibre-dimension-flat] show that $R_{\mathfrak p}\to B'_{\mathfrak q'}$ is flat and that $B'_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then [lem-weil-pbc-flat-smooth-fibre-smooth-at-prime], with (1) $B'$ finitely presented ($g=1$), (2) this flatness, (3) = (b), shows that $R\to B'$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q'$: there is $g'\in B'\setminus\mathfrak q'$ with $B'_{g'}$ smooth over $R$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_desingularization_quotient_data (R : Type u) (Λ : Type v) (A : Type w) [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ] [CommRing A] [Algebra R Λ] [Algebra R A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [FinitePresentation R A] (π : R) (α : A →ₐ[R] Λ) (hΛ : ∀ l : Λ, l * algebraMap R Λ π = 0 ↔ l * (algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2 = 0) (hstandard : IsStrictlyStandardElement (R := R) (algebraMap R A π)) (hρ : ∃ ρ : (A ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R A π) ^ 4}) →ₐ[R] (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 4}), ∀ (a : A) (r : R), ρ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ r → Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 4}) (α a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 4}) (algebraMap R Λ r)) : ∃ (S : Type (max u w)) (_ : CommRing S) (_ : Algebra R S), FinitePresentation R S ∧ ∃ K : Ideal S, K ≤ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R S π) ^ 2} ∧ Ideal.span {algebraMap R S π} * K ≤ K ^ 2 ∧ FinitePresentation R (S ⧸ K) ∧ ∃ (β : (S ⧸ K) →ₐ[R] Λ) (aB : A →ₐ[R] (S ⧸ K)), β.comp aB = α ∧ Smooth R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R (S ⧸ K) π)) ∧ ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S, algebraMap R S π ∈ q.asIdeal → IsSmoothAtPrime R q ∧ Module.Flat R (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
